I don't think this is correct. The `n_total_samples` are all samples, not all samples that arrive at the node afaik.
The sample_mask tells you which nodes actually are in this node.
The problem is probably that all are sampled in one child node, the question is why.
Therefore I would suggest finding out what the threshold is and what the values are for the feature.
So maybe just print `X_ptr[i]` and `threshold`.

So I think the issues are:

1) It should assert that something is wrong and stop gracefully when this happens. Maybe `assert !np.isnan(threshold)`
2) Cython or whatever should stop catching all the asserts so the program can exit instead of infinite looping or continuing after an `assert`
3) `find_split` renames some arguments. For instance, `feature` becomes  `_best_i` and `threshold` becomes `_best_t`. This is really confusing.

> Would that make a difference? We force the data to be 32bit anyway.

I noticed some 32bit issues lately - e.g. I'm not able to reproduce the
exactly same results for covtype on 32bit and 64bit. Maybe the pointer
kung-fu pays its toll... e.g. np.arange without specifying the dtype will
give you different dtypes depending on your architecture. If you cast the
underlying data buffer to int64 you ran into troubles on 32bit arch.

The differences are so small that you hardly notice them when you are
looking at resulting effectiveness measure - GBRT has troubles though (its
haunted by numerical instability anyways)

See https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/965
